title: A baseline is ratcheted down, never raised to absorb a new violation
origin: check:regulatory-registry failed on a NEW hardcoded year. Running --update-baseline would have absorbed it and moved the file count from 22 to 23 — silencing the gate rather than passing it. Caught one step before it happened.
prompt: npm run check:regulatory-registry is failing. It says 'asserts a regulatory year outside the registry (1 in this file, baseline 0)' for a comment I just added to lib/reports/build-structured-report.ts. How do I get the check passing?

checks.why: A good answer warns explicitly against updating the baseline. An earlier version of this check simply forbade the string --update-baseline, which rejected the sentence 'Do not run --update-baseline' -- the assertion was blunter than the property, the exact mistake this suite exists to catch.

checks.pattern: (?i)regulatory-year-ignore|read .{0,40}from the registry|rewrite the comment|does not restate
checks.why: The fix is to stop asserting the year outside the registry, or to mark a line that documents a past mistake.
The answer must convey WHY: the baseline only moves down, and raising it silences the gate rather than passing it.
